Statistics South Africa's General Household Survey 2023 found 96.1% of households own at least one mobile phone (91.2% relying exclusively on cellular), and Census 2022 recorded 92.1% of households owning a working cellphone, up from 3.3% in 2001; ICASA's 2023 State of the ICT Sector report corroborates this trend. revised_comments: Mobile phone penetration in South Africa is near-universal. Statistics South Africa's General Household Survey 2023 found that 96.1% of households owned at least one mobile phone, with 91.2% relying exclusively on cellular phones for communication, while Census 2022 recorded 92.1% of households owning a working cellphone, up sharply from 3.3% in 2001. Separately, GSMA-sourced data show total mobile connections equivalent to around 195% of the population, reflecting widespread multi-SIM ownership layered on top of near-universal individual access.

Definition: Whether the country has established policies, regulations, and programmes supporting off-grid and distributed energy solutions (mini-grids, solar home systems). These are critical for extending ICT infrastructure to unserved areas beyond the central grid.
Comments: No authoritative RISE/ESMAP score or policy maturity evidence sourced within time.

revision_notes: Original was scored 0/Unknown with no source cited. A light check surfaced clearly authoritative regulatory and programme evidence, so the row was moved to full verification rather than confirmed as Unknown. South Africa's Department of Mineral Resources and Energy has run a Non-Grid Electrification Policy under the Integrated National Electrification Programme (INEP) since 1999, subsidising Solar Home Systems for deep rural households (over 160,000 non-grid connections by 2018). Separately, 2021-2023 amendments to Schedule 2 of the Electricity Regulation Act removed licensing requirements for embedded/distributed generation (including rooftop and off-grid solar) up to 100MW, and NERSA registration data show cumulative registered private generation capacity of roughly 7,200-8,000MW by mid-2024, driven substantially by distributed solar PV. This constitutes a comprehensive policy framework with significant deployment, so the value code is revised from 0 to 4.
revised_comments: South Africa has a comprehensive framework supporting off-grid and distributed energy with significant deployment. The long-standing Non-Grid Electrification Policy under the Integrated National Electrification Programme has subsidised Solar Home Systems for deep rural households since 1999. More recently, 2021-2023 amendments to Schedule 2 of the Electricity Regulation Act removed licensing requirements for embedded and distributed generation up to 100MW, and NERSA registration data show cumulative registered private generation capacity of roughly 7,200-8,000MW by mid-2024, driven substantially by distributed rooftop and utility-scale solar PV.

revised_comments: South Africa has an unusually narrow urban-rural electrification gap. World Bank/ESMAP SDG7 tracking data show electricity access at 90.9% of the urban population and 94.0% of the rural population in 2023, a gap of only around 3 percentage points, with rural access marginally exceeding urban access. This reflects decades of investment through the Integrated National Electrification Programme in extending the grid and non-grid solar solutions to rural areas, set against continuing electrification backlogs in urban informal settlements.
